## Description

Free-living amoeba of soil and water. The trophozoite measures 15–45 µm and extends acanthopodia
(thin, spine-like pseudopods). It eats bacteria and yeasts and forms very resistant cysts, also
against heat. It is a model organism for phagocytosis and an opportunistic pathogen (keratitis,
granulomatous encephalitis). It grows best near 32 °C and encysts above ~36 °C.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 4 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A small plastic-membrane amoeba (~30 µm) that phagocytoses bacteria by contact. Small plastic
amoebae use finer remeshing and a relaxed cortex during cytokinesis so that the furrow closes.

## Not implemented yet

- Acanthopodia are not distinguished from ordinary lobose pseudopods.
- Encystment is not triggered by temperature above ~36 °C; the double-walled cyst is not drawn.
- No intracellular bacteria (*Legionella*) or pathogenicity.
- The µmax temperature is not verified.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Shares the [plastic membrane and phagocytic cup](../../mechanics/feeding-and-phagocytosis.md) with *Amoeba*,
*Chaos* and *Naegleria*, and the [cysts](../../mechanics/life-cycle-and-division.md). Its division unlocked the
fix for small plastic amoebae (fine remeshing during cytokinesis).
